cook.date: 2026-11-02 (House & Senate final ratings); 2026-10-27 (Governor final ratings; Wikipedia table labels it Oct 29)
cook.notes: cookpolitical.com returns 403 to scripted fetches and Wayback content fetch was rate-blocked. Ratings taken from Wikipedia prediction tables (Senate col dated Nov 2, House Nov 2, Gov Oct 29) and cross-checked race-by-race against 270toWin Cook maps (Senate/Gov maps labelled "November 2: Final 2026 ratings"; House table "As of November 2, 2026"): 100% agreement. Final House update (Nov 2) shifted FL-4, NC-7, NC-14, TN-9, VA-5 toward Dems (Wasserman). Final Senate update (Nov 2) moved Michigan Toss Up -> Lean D. Final Governor update (Oct 27, Substack "final 2026 CPR Governor Race Ratings"): Kansas Lean R -> Toss Up, Nebraska Likely R -> Lean R.

sabato.notes: "THE FINAL 2026 RATINGS: Democrats Favored to Capture House, Senate, and Gubernatorial Majorities" (Kondik & Coleman), Mon Nov 2, 2026. Yes: Toss-ups eliminated in every chamber; zero Toss-ups remain in Wikipedia and 270toWin Sabato tables. House: "leaned the bulk of the final Toss-ups to Democrats", last batch broke 14-3 to Leans D. Senate: Iowa was "the one Toss-up race where we feel the best about Republicans" -> Leans R; Kansas, Texas, Ohio, Maine -> Leans D. Governors: GA and NV (the only Toss-ups) -> Leans D; Alaska Leans D -> Likely D; NH added to Leans R; Louisiana Senate flagged Leans R. centerforpolitics.org returns 403; ratings from Wikipedia + 270toWin (100% agreement), text via Substack copy.

inside.notes: Final ratings released the week of Oct 26 (Wikipedia & 270toWin House table: Oct 29, 2026); Roll Call (Oct 31) "Final rating changes: 63 races move toward Democrats, 1 toward Republicans" lists all 64 changes (45 House, 9 Senate, 10 Gov). 270toWin labels its IE Senate/Gov maps "November 2: Final 2026 ratings" (likely 270toWin's entry date; ratings identical). No IE update after Oct 29 found. insideelections.com returns 403; ratings from Wikipedia + 270toWin (100% agreement), changes confirmed against Roll Call list.

conventions.rating_text: Ratings in rater-native wording (Cook/IE: Solid/Likely/Lean/Tilt(IE only)/Toss-up; Sabato: Safe/Likely/Lean/Toss-up). Cook publishes "Toss Up" and Sabato "Leans"; normalized here to "Toss-up"/"Lean".
conventions.flip: "(flip)" is the Wikipedia table annotation meaning the favored party differs from the seat's current holder; not part of the rater's label.
conventions.source_values: "wiki + 270toWin rater maps (agree)" = Wikipedia final predictions table cross-checked against 270toWin per-rater final maps; every race matched in all three chambers. Rater websites (cookpolitical.com, centerforpolitics.org, insideelections.com) all returned 403 to scripted fetches and Wayback content was blocked, so no race was read directly off a rater ratings page; rater-published text (Substack, X posts, Roll Call for IE) was used to confirm dates, final changes and chamber calls.
conventions.changed_from_mid_oct: Compared after stripping dates/(flip)/Solid-vs-Safe wording. Some stored mid-Oct values were already stale (e.g. dated Apr 2025), so a listed change may predate mid-October.
